All key premises—from the feasibility of laser surface alloying of borides with silicon, to the specific reaction forming a silicide barrier, to its efficacy against molten aluminum corrosion—are specific claims requiring experimental support, yet none is provided.
premises: Silicon can be introduced into the near-surface region of boride-based components via laser surface alloying.
Added silicon reacts with the boride surface at high temperature to form a stable, self-healing silicide phase.
The formed Si-rich (silicide) interfacial layer acts as a diffusion barrier against molten aluminum.
This diffusion barrier reduces corrosion attack (penetration and weight loss) in molten aluminum at 700–800 °C.
